messages:
raj: Heads-up — after the 6.3 kernel + driver roll yesterday in eu-west2, we've seen intermittent GPU peer-connect failures and some pods OOMing during multi-GPU workloads. Not full outage but tail latency and memory blowups on Ampere nodes.
ops-bot: deploybot: kernel-upgrade job completed on eu-west2-gpu-pool at 2025-11-03T01:05Z :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: nodes affected: 6/120 rolled, 6/6 reporting driver 535.104 + kernel 6.3.2
natalie: Got it. Any specific error from containers? logs?
raj: Sample from training pod: 
```
I tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:XXX] failed to enable P2P: peerAccessEnable returned error: 38
nvidia-smi topo --matrix shows NVLink up for some pairs, missing for others
```
raj: dmesg on a host shows repeated BAR1/vbar1 warnings and ACS enforcement messages around the driver init.
tj: ACS enforcement + BAR1 warnings smell like PCIe hotplug/ACS kernel enforcement change. Did the distro flip a default?
maria: I pulled the node-exporter metrics — scatter of nvlink errors around the kernel reboot window, and io_wait spikes on the same hosts.
natalie: Can you paste the exact dmesg lines? might help confirm whether it's kernel ACS enforcement vs a driver regression.
raj: paste: 
```
[  +0.123456] pci 0000:3b:00.0: enabling Device-PCIe-ACS
[  +0.000123] pcieport 0000:3b:00.0: PCIe ACS: Request to enable ACS for peer-to-peer
[  +0.000045] nvidia: BAR1 size mismatch: expected 0x6000000 got 0x4000000
[  +0.000067] nvidia: p2p_init: peeraccess failed, disabling p2p for gpu-pair
```
raj: Also saw one host drop NVLink negotiation at runtime and report HOT_RESET events.
tj: Ok — two hypotheses: 1) kernel 6.3 tightened ACS enforcement causing BAR1/peeraccess negotiation to fail, or 2) new driver 535.x has changed BAR1 probing assumptions for Ampere and misreads sizing on some OEM boards.
maria: Which hardware variants? We have both A100 40GB and A100 80GB in that pool. I see the failures only on 40GB hosts so far.
natalie: Good detail. If it's a BAR1 size mismatch it's likely firmware/BIOS tables + driver interaction. Can we repro by booting a canary with older driver + new kernel and vice versa?
raj: I'm spinning two canaries now: (A) kernel 6.2 + driver 535.104, (B) kernel 6.3 + driver 530.41. Will post results in ~15m.
natalie: In the meantime, let's avoid mass roll in eu-west2 and pause the remaining batch. Marked the job paused in the rollout dashboard.
natalie: @tj can you also check if kube-device-plugin logs show any failed NVML initializations? Could cause pods to try weird fallbacks and OOM.
tj: Looking — yes, device-plugin on node-12 shows: "Failed to query BAR1 size for GPU 1: -22" then device-plugin re-registers, kubelet briefly evicts GPU pods.
maria: Cost note — if we need to roll back to older driver we might burn extra hours on reserved capacity while re-draining; estimate ~12 node-hours across the pool if we rollback en masse. Decision on rollback should weigh risk of more OOMs vs cost.
natalie: Agreed. For now: pause rollout, cordon the 6/6 affected nodes, schedule narrow rollback canary (driver 530 on one 40GB node), run synthetic p2p test (nvlink topo + CUDA sample p2pBandwidthLatency).
natalie: Test script (quick): 
```
# on host
modprobe nvidia
nvidia-smi topo --matrix
cuda-p2p-bw-test --gpu0 0 --gpu1 1
```
raj: Canary B (6.3 + 530.41) booted — initial result: nvlink shows full connectivity, p2pBandwidthLatency passes. Canary A (6.2 + 535.104) fails with same BAR1 mismatch.
ops-bot: alert: rollback recommended for driver 535.104 on A100-40GB flavor — see rollback-run-1959876100
tj: That points to driver 535 interacting poorly with 40GB A100 on our OEM BIOS + kernel combo. We'll need to open ticket with vendor + NVIDIA.
maria: Also flagging cost/throughput mitigation: route customer traffic away from eu-west2-gpu-pool to other regions for heavy multi-GPU jobs until we fix. We have capacity in us-west3 but cross-region egress costs and latency tradeoffs.
natalie: I'll notify Support and SRE to create a customer-facing note if we need region-level routing. Keep this thread for updates.
raj: For postmortem: capture exact PCI device tree (lspci -vv), dmesg, driver versions, BIOS rev, and nvlink topo. I'll collect from the affected hosts and attach.
tj: I'll open vendor/NVIDIA ticket with logs and mark it P0.
maria: Quick mitigation steps agreed: pause rollout, cordon affected nodes, run driver rollback on a small canary set of 3 nodes (40GB A100), and traffic-shift plan drafted.
natalie: Thanks. If anyone sees additional hosts with BAR1 mismatch, post hostnames here and don't drain them yet until we have rollback tested. :eyes:
